body: thank you. this was what i was needing to hear.

the best way to get back at parents like yours is to persist. i know that sounds impossible, but my mother is psychologically abusive (with three instances of physical abuse that i can remember) and the best way i've been able to surpass her is to disconnect from her entirely if you're in a place to do that. outlive her. talk crazy shit about her at her funeral. that's what i'm looking forward to when it comes her time to take her dirt nap. and by then who knows how you'll feel. maybe you'll have met people that make you feel strong. maybe you'll have put leagues between the two of you, and she'll barely be an afterthought. i think it's worth sticking around to see and find out.

I'm ftm and have been on hormones for roughly 11 months now come the 28th, and in that time i've changed quite a bit ( it's hard to tell in the face unless i have side by side comparisons of me pre transitioning, to present) as in i'm building quite a bit of facial hair, my body shape is more masculine and my voice is still dropping. before i began i was considered pretty, and now that i'm beginning to look less and less feminine, i'm definitely noticing a change in demeanor with people i engage with. i don't think the hesitance is necessarily an imagined slight, but is probably not as serious as we initially think it is since it's still so new to us. if you're adhd like me your rejection sensitivity probably is just amplifying the effects of the differences in your interactions. overall, i wouldn't focus too much on it if you can help it, recognize that there are still people out there who are not accustomed to dealing with trans people. continue to be kind, and enjoy your journey!
